lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: fitting a function to bivariate data and assessing fit with residual plots
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: fitting a function to bivariate data and assessing fit with residual plots

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: Row 1 has 12 yes and 8 no. Fraction of row 1 saying yes?
For ŷ = 4x + 60, interpret the slope where x is hours studied.

steps: Slope is change in y per unit x.
One more hour is associated with about 4 more points.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.

items.prompt: A data set records 9, 16, 11, 5, 2. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 9, median 9
mean 8.6, median 9
mean 9, median 8.6
mean 8.6, median 11

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 173 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 29 yes, 18 no; row 2: 34 yes, 27 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 7x + 45, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 7 test points.
The predicted value is 7 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 7 test points.
Each additional test points is associated with 7 more hour studieds.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

items.prompt: A data set records 36, 2, 10, 23, 37, 28, 36. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 24.57, median 28
mean 25, median 28
mean 28, median 24.57
mean 24.57, median 25

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 309 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
